problems: stop 2 card 11, answer 1: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: Elimelech takes his family across the border to live in Moab when the famine hits home, as Ruth 1:1 tells us. That land becomes their new home for years.
Some families headed for Egypt in famine times down the road of Bible history, but this family goes to Moab, according to Ruth 1:1.
Edom sits down south, but Elimelech leads his family toward Moab, as Ruth 1:1 points out.
The text names her right there in Ruth 1:4, the Moabite woman whose name is on this whole book of the Bible.
Rachel is a name from way back in Genesis, but the son's wife here is Ruth, as Ruth 1:4 states.
Dinah shows up in the stories of Jacob's family, but the Moabite wife in Ruth 1:4 is Ruth.
After her husband goes, both Mahlon and Chilion pass away too, leaving Naomi entirely on her own in Moab, as Ruth 1:5 records.

explanations.answer: Her house in Moab burns down
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention any fire. Ruth 1:5 simply records the heavy sorrow of both sons dying after about ten years.

explanations.answer: She falls sick and loses her sight
explanations.explanation: Naomi faces the deep grief of losing her husband and both sons, as Ruth 1:5 tells us, not a sickness of her own.
Naomi hears that the LORD has attended to His people by providing them with food, as Ruth 1:6 states, and that news sets her feet back toward Judah.
The time of the judges was long before Israel had kings sitting in Jerusalem, but here the LORD provides food, according to Ruth 1:6.
The news from home isn't about a battle won, but about the LORD providing food for His people, as Ruth 1:6 points out.

explanations.answer: Go back to their mothers' homes
explanations.explanation: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to turn back to their own mothers' homes so they can find new lives, as Ruth 1:8 records.

explanations.answer: Walk faster to beat the dark
explanations.explanation: She isn't worried about the sunset on the road. Ruth 1:8 shows her telling them to head back home to their families.

explanations.answer: Stay close to her the whole way
explanations.explanation: Naomi actually tells them the opposite, urging them in Ruth 1:8 to turn around and go back to where they came from.
Naomi tells them in Ruth 1:9, 'May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.'
Ruth 1:9 actually has Naomi wishing them rest in the home of a new husband.

explanations.answer: We will return with you to your people
explanations.explanation: Both daughters-in-law tell her right away that they will go back with her to her people, as Ruth 1:10 records.

explanations.answer: We will stay in Moab and wait for you
explanations.explanation: They don't offer to stay behind. Ruth 1:10 states they tell her they are going with her.

explanations.answer: We will come visit you in Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: They aren't talking about a casual visit, but walking right along with her, as Ruth 1:10 shows.

explanations.answer: Would you wait for them to grow up
explanations.explanation: Naomi asks if they would really sit around and wait for brand-new sons to grow up, as Ruth 1:13 records.

explanations.answer: Would you raise them as your own
explanations.explanation: She doesn't ask about raising children, but whether they would wait for them to grow up, according to Ruth 1:13.

explanations.answer: Would you go ahead to Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: That travel plan isn't in her question. Ruth 1:13 shows her asking if they would wait for any new sons to grow up.

explanations.answer: The LORD's hand has turned against her
explanations.explanation: Naomi tells them it is much more bitter for her because the hand of the LORD has gone out against her, as Ruth 1:13 states.

explanations.answer: The people of Judah have turned against her
explanations.explanation: She isn't talking about the townspeople yet, but says in Ruth 1:13 that the hand of the LORD has gone out against her.

explanations.answer: The people of Moab have turned against her
explanations.explanation: Moab isn't the source of her bitterness in this verse. Ruth 1:13 points straight to the hand of the LORD.
Ruth 1:14 tells us that Orpah kisses her mother-in-law goodbye and turns back.
Ruth 1:14 plainly states that Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye.
Ruth doesn't go back with Orpah; Ruth 1:14 says she clings to Naomi instead.
Ruth stays right by Naomi's side and clings to her, as Ruth 1:14 records, while Orpah heads back.
Naomi points out that Orpah went back to her people and her gods, and tells Ruth in Ruth 1:15 to follow her back home.
Ruth 1:15 shows Naomi telling Ruth to follow her sister-in-law back home.

explanations.answer: Naomi's God will be her God
explanations.explanation: Ruth makes that famous promise in Ruth 1:16, telling Naomi that her people will be her people and her God will be her God.

explanations.answer: She will take care of Naomi's house
explanations.explanation: She promises her life to Naomi rather than just housekeeping, declaring in Ruth 1:16 that Naomi's God will be her God.

explanations.answer: She will learn all the ways of Judah
explanations.explanation: Ruth commits herself entirely to Naomi's people and says in Ruth 1:16 that Naomi's God will be her God.
Ruth swears in Ruth 1:17 that may the LORD punish her if anything but death separates her and Naomi.
Distance doesn't stop Ruth. Ruth 1:17 says nothing can separate them except death itself.
Ruth isn't talking about marriage separating them, but vows in Ruth 1:17 that only death will come between them.

explanations.answer: She stops trying to persuade her
explanations.explanation: When Naomi sees that Ruth is completely determined to go with her, Ruth 1:18 says she stops trying to persuade her.

explanations.answer: She sends her back after Orpah
explanations.explanation: Naomi stops arguing once she sees Ruth's heart, as Ruth 1:18 records.

explanations.answer: She tells her to wait in Moab
explanations.explanation: Ruth goes right along with her because Naomi stops trying to change her mind, according to Ruth 1:18.
The whole town gets stirred up when they walk in, and the women exclaim, 'Can this be Naomi?' as Ruth 1:19 records.
They don't ask about Elimelech right off the bat; Ruth 1:19 shows them asking, 'Can this be Naomi?'
They recognize her enough to be shocked, asking in Ruth 1:19, 'Can this be Naomi?'
Naomi tells them not to call her Naomi anymore, but to call her Mara because the Almighty has dealt bitterly with her, as Ruth 1:20 states.
Hannah is another faithful woman in Scripture, but Naomi asks the town to call her Mara, according to Ruth 1:20.
Leah belongs to the earlier stories of Genesis, whereas Naomi chooses the name Mara in Ruth 1:20.
Naomi says the exact opposite in Ruth 1:21, stating that she went away full and the LORD brought her back empty.
Naomi tells them in Ruth 1:21 that she went away full and came back empty, making this statement false.
They arrive in Bethlehem right at the beginning of the barley harvest, as Ruth 1:22 tells us, setting the stage for what happens next.
Wheat comes later in the season, but Ruth 1:22 specifies they arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.
The text doesn't mention an olive harvest here. Ruth 1:22 points straight to the barley harvest.
